title: Choose the GlucoBar icon direction (safer hand)
question: Safer register: three familiar macOS-utility directions, plus the category standard. No roll leads this round; take whichever fits.

options.label: Instrument Gauge
options.thesis: A graphite dial whose widened white arc is the target range; a green needle sits inside it, the Reading below.
options.viewport: A 220-degree dial; the in-range zone is a thicker, brighter arc, so range reads by shape, not just colour.
options.risk: Reads as a speed test or CPU monitor; the number under the hub vanishes below 64 px.

options.label: Trend Arrow
options.thesis: One bold white Trend arrow, rising, on a warm amber squircle: 'where am I heading' as the whole mark.
options.viewport: A single 45-degree arrow centred, with a soft shadow lifting it off the field.
options.risk: Generic: the same arrow means 'open link' or 'export' in many apps, and says nothing about glucose until learned.

options.label: G Monogram
options.thesis: A rounded G whose crossbar runs out as a mint Trend arrow, white on indigo.
options.viewport: The G fills the squircle; its crossbar breaks out of the letter as an arrow.
options.risk: Can read as a 'log in' or 'go' symbol; a lettermark says GlucoBar only to people who already know it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A CGM trace threading a target band on a blue-teal gradient squircle, built to the polish of menu bar peers like iStat Menus, Fantastical and Bartender.
canonCard.viewport: A wavy glucose line crossing a pale in-range band, ending in a dot.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every diabetes app and reads clinical.
